'''Susanoo Shrine (Fukuyama)''' is a shrine in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Bingo Province]].

'''Susanoo Shrine''' (素盞嗚神社, ''Susanoo Jinja'') is a [[Shinto]] shrine located in {{ill|Fukuyama, Hiroshima|en|Fukuyama, Hiroshima|qid=Q661038|lt=Shin'ichi Town, Fukuyama City}}, [[Hiroshima Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It is classified as a [[Shikinaisha]] and claims to be the [[Ichinomiya]] of {{ill|Bingo Province|en|Bingo Province|qid=Q1049113|lt=Bingo Province}}. The shrine was formerly designated as a [[Kensha|Prefectural Shrine]] under the [[modern shrine Ranking system]]. Known for its [[Gion Faith|Gion faith]] and as the origin of the [[Gion Matsuri]], the shrine's grounds are said to have been the site of the mansion of the mythical giant [[Somin Shorai]].

== Deities ==
; Main deity
* '''[[Susanoo no Mikoto|Susanoo-no-Mikoto]]''' (素盞嗚尊)

; Associated Deities
* '''[[Kushinadahime|Inadahime no Mikoto]]''' (稲田姫命) – Consort of Susanoo
* '''[[:en:Hachioji|Yahashira no Mikogami]]''' (八柱御子) – Offspring of Susanoo

== History ==
According to the shrine's tradition, it was established during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|en|Emperor Tenmu|qid=Q335181|lt=Emperor Tenmu}} in the 7th century (around {{ill|679|en|679|qid=Q3599607|lt=679}}). Later, the [[Tang dynasty]] envoy [[Kibi no Makibi]] is said to have brought the deity from {{ill|Bingo Province|en|Bingo Province|qid=Q1049113|lt=Bingo Province}} to {{ill|Harima Province|en|Harima Province|qid=Q1047523|lt=Harima Province}}’s [[Hiromine Shrine]] in {{ill|734|en|734|qid=Q23573|lt=734}}.

The shrine is mentioned in a quote from the now-lost ''[[Bingo no Kuni Fudoki]]'' (circa Nara period) within ''[[Shaku Nihongi]]'' (compiled in the Kamakura period), as "Enokuma Kuni-tsu Yashiro" (疫隈國社), though some believe this refers to its auxiliary shrine, Somin Shrine and Hōsō Shrine. It is listed in the ''[[Engishiki]]'' as "Susanoo-no-Mikoto Shrine" in the ''Shikinaisha'' of [[Fukatsu District, Bingo Province|Fukatsu District, Bingo Province]].

During the [[syncretism of Shinto and Buddhism]], the shrine adopted [[Gozu Tennō]] as its deity and was renamed "Hayasayama Tenryūin Tennōji." The main hall (*hondō*), known as the Honchi Hall (now Tenmangū), housed the {{ill|Bodhisattva|en|Bodhisattva|qid=Q178149|lt=Bodhisattva}} [[Kannon]] as its main deity, flanked by [[Acala]] and [[:en:Bishamonten|Bishamonten]]. Following the [[Meiji Restoration]] and the [[Shinbutsu bunri|separation of Shinto and Buddhism]], the shrine reverted to its original deity, Susanoo-no-Mikoto, and was renamed to its current designation.

== Grounds ==
; Main Hall
* [[File:素盞嗚神社 (福山市新市町戸手) 本殿.JPG|thumb|200px|Main Hall]]
* Built in [[irimoya-zukuri]] style with a cypress bark roof. It is said to have been reconstructed by [[Mizuno Katsunari]], the first lord of Bingo Fukuyama Domain.

; '''Heiden''' (Offering Hall)
* Connects the main hall and the worship hall.

; '''Naki Ryū''' ("Crying Dragon")
* A rare acoustic feature shared by only about 20 buildings in Japan.

; Sacred Cedar ("Jindai no Sugi")
* Once stood at the northeast corner of the grounds as a sacred tree. A stone monument marks its location.

== Subsidiary Shrines ==
; Somin Shrine and Hōsō Shrine
[[File:蘇民神社 (素盞嗚神社 福山市新市町戸手 境内社).JPG|thumb|200px|Somin and Hōsō Shrines]]
* Located south of the main hall, these are considered to be the original "Enokuma Kuni-tsu Yashiro" of the ''Bingo no Kuni Fudoki.'' According to legend, the shrine sits on the site of the giant [[Somin Shorai]]’s mansion.

; Tode Tenmangū
[[File:戸手天満宮 (素盞嗚神社 福山市新市町戸手 境内社).JPG|thumb|200px|Tode Tenmangū]]
* Originally the Honchi Hall of the temple "Tenryūin Tennōji," it was converted into a Tenmangū during the [[Meiji period]].

== Festivals ==
; Gion Matsuri
The Gion Matsuri, locally referred to as "Gion-san" or "Tenno-san," is an annual festival held in July, featuring mikoshi processions from nearby communities. The festival includes "Mikoshi-Awase," a vigorous display of mikoshi parading.

== Access ==
* '''Train:''' 3-minute walk from [[Kamitoide Station]] on the [[JR West]] {{ill|Fukuen Line|en|Fukuen Line|qid=Q899394|lt=Fukuen Line}}.
* '''Bus:''' From {{ill|Fukuyama Station|en|Fukuyama Station|qid=Q800797|lt=Fukuyama Station}}, take a [[Chugoku Bus]] to "Teraoka Memorial Hospital," then walk 5 minutes.
== See Also ==
* [[Gion Faith|Gion faith]]
* [[Kibitsu Shrine]] in Fukuyama, also considered Bingo Province's Ichinomiya.

== External Links ==
* [https://www.k-shinichi.com/spot?id=7 Susanoo Shrine] (Shin'ichi Town Tourism Association)
